key_insight: Decision models can handle structured clinical subtasks cheaply, while LLMs remain stronger for harder or less certain cases.
clinical_relevance: A hybrid workflow that routes confident structured decisions to a decision model and the rest to an LLM could reduce cost without sacrificing performance.
method: Compared a decision model (Jev) with five flagship LLMs on three clinical tasks.
Tasks included mortality risk prediction, Choosing-Wisely category decisions, and ordinal colon cancer staging.
Tested standard prompting plus developer-guided input changes such as added context and task decomposition.
evidence_signal: On standard inputs, Jev underperformed LLMs, but with improved prompting it reached 75.8% to 85.8% staging accuracy; routing only fully confident staging cases to Jev made the hybrid approach non-inferior and cut LLM costs by 33% to 44%.
watch_item: The hybrid approach depends on reliable confidence calibration and may not transfer equally well across tasks or settings without careful validation.
paper_title: Decision models can offload structured clinical tasks from large language models
